verdicts.reason: Designing measurement and feedback loops is a distinct behavior from analyzing failure conditions and safeguards; a comment can propose reporting metrics with no failure analysis at all.
Spotting an over-inclusive category the rule conflates requires no reference to any other rule or docket, which is exactly what the second criterion demands.
A commenter can supply load-bearing numbers from their own operations with no external citation, and can cite a locatable study containing no quantities that carry the argument.
The second criterion additionally requires anchoring the change to an identified proposed provision, so a precise but unanchored threshold proposal scores high on the first and low on the second.
Both score a traced step-by-step chain from the proposal to concrete consequences and both zero out on bare assertions of help or harm; the wording differs, not the concept.
Rebutting an objection with reasoning and supplying a workable substitute policy are separate acts; a comment can do either without the other.
Pinpointing and explaining the proposal's own provisions is not the same as identifying governing statutory or precedential language and applying it.
Laying out how the proposal as written could be executed differs from proposing a different design; a detailed implementation path may endorse the rule unchanged.
Proposing prospective monitoring and triggers is distinct from quantifying effects against a baseline, and comments routinely do one without the other.
Weighing competing objectives and explaining a preferred balance is separable from offering a concrete substitute approach when objecting.
Correcting an error or ambiguity in the agency's wording is not the same as specifying an exact requested action; a precise request may identify no textual defect.
Both reward applying identified statutory, regulatory, or precedential language to the proposal and both zero out on legal conclusions asserted without textual support.
A single clean causal chain to a direct effect scores high on mechanism while scoring low on cross-system and second-order spillovers.

The steelman criterion requires the opposing rationale in its strongest form and an answer on its own terms, so thorough engagement with a weak objection scores high on the broader counter-argument criterion and mid on this one.
Distributional incidence is about who bears unequal costs and benefits, whereas edge-case coverage is about contexts where the rule operates differently, including non-population contexts.
A developed ultra-vires argument requires no CFR part and section citations, and a comment full of CFR citations may make no authority argument.
Pinpointing a proposed provision and requesting a revision is distinct from reasoning from governing legal text.
Calibrated partial agreement measures how cleanly accepted parts are separated from disputed ones, a rhetorical posture absent from mere provision-level targeting.

The ambiguity criterion demands two rival readings and their divergent consequences, while the correction criterion also credits flagging factual errors or misstatements with a single correct reading.
Rule-specific numbers can appear in a purely diagnostic comment that requests no specific action, and a precise request can carry no numbers.
Steelmanning and answering the best contrary argument is narrower than recognizing competing objectives, comparing them, and defending a balance.
Proposing an alternative design and proposing measurement or verification machinery are separate contributions.
A comment can supply a fully specified alternative without weighing competing objectives, and can weigh tradeoffs without proposing any alternative.
Both score whether concrete firsthand or local observation is lifted into a rule-relevant generalizable implication, and both zero out on unanalyzed anecdote.
Identifying a distinction the rule conflates is internal to this rule; cross-rule consistency concerns interactions and duplication across other rules and agencies.
Targeting proposed rule text with a revision is not the same as connecting the proposal to statutory authority and legal limits.
Conflation of sub-cases is a defect internal to the rule, whereas conflict identification requires naming another instrument and an inconsistency with it.
Laying out a behavioral causal chain is one-directional argumentation and does not require acknowledging or answering any opposing consideration.
Requesting a concrete revision to a named provision does not require identifying any conflated category, and vice versa.
Gap analysis targets what the proposal fails to say, while pinpointing targets what it does say and how to revise it.
Failure-mode analysis is oriented to things going wrong and to safeguards, while edge-case coverage is oriented to heterogeneous contexts and populations where the rule operates differently.
An unaddressed scenario in this rule's text can be raised with no comparison to any other rule or docket.
Offering a substitute approach is not the same as stating and answering the strongest contrary rationale.
A comment can pinpoint a provision and demand a different threshold without identifying any error, ambiguity, or misstatement in the agency's wording.
The first is a compound that also scores critique of evidence quality and contrary evidence, so a comment that attacks the agency's studies but never hedges its own claims splits the two.
Both score whether the requested change is specified as exact text, thresholds, definitions, or concrete steps rather than a vague directional ask, with matching zero anchors.
Correcting the operative rule text differs from engaging the preamble's rationale, cost analysis, and cited studies; a comment can do either alone.
Answering an objection to one's own position is not the same as explicitly weighing benefits, costs, risks, and affected parties against each other.
Rule-specific numbers and cross-referencing another identified rule or docket are unrelated contributions.
The omission criterion is broader than unaddressed scenarios, covering undelivered commitments and unassigned responsibilities that involve no edge-case scenario at all.
Targeting a provision for revision does not require identifying any interaction, conflict, or duplication across rules or agencies.
Both score supplying self-derived monetary compliance-burden figures with the basis stated, and both zero out when no figures appear.
Supplying rule-specific numbers and identifying a provision with a concrete revision are independent behaviors.
Correcting the proposal's own wording requires no comparison to another rule, docket, or precedent.
Both score proposing concrete measurement, data collection, monitoring, or validation procedures, and both zero out on vague calls for more study or oversight.

Both hinge on naming a specific other instrument and reasoning about its relation to the proposal, with identical zero anchors of treating the rule in isolation; the conflict-versus-consistency framing rarely changes the ranking.
Both score whether a concrete, workable alternative that still serves the agency's objective is offered, and both zero out on bare rejection.
Identifying which groups bear risks does not require naming a specific place, facility, or institution, which the second criterion makes the core requirement.
The second criterion requires the named instance to cut against a premise the agency relies on, while the first credits any specific real case adduced in support.
Cross-system spillovers are about breadth of effects while dynamic consequences are about time horizon, adaptation, and cumulation.
Quantitative specificity and legal textual reasoning are unrelated dimensions.
The first is a compound that also credits recognizing and answering objections to one's own position, so pure objection handling with no cost-benefit weighing splits the two.
Weighing tradeoffs is unrelated to focus, ranking of recommendations, and decision-readiness.
The first additionally requires explicit comparison of competing objectives and a defended balance, which a comment that merely rebuts one objection does not supply.
Rebutting an objection is the opposite move from conceding a real limitation of one's own position, and a strong rebuttal concedes nothing.
Near-verbatim restatements: both score identifiable studies, records, or data relevant to the proposal versus unsupported assertion.
Textual correction and rule-specific quantification are independent contributions.

The second requires firsthand operational detail of the existing workflow and where the rule breaks, while the first credits a forward-looking path with actors, resources, transition, and timing that an outsider can lay out.
Describing one's own regulated practice and expressing intense feeling are unrelated, and the second explicitly scores register rather than substance.
Naming a provision and requesting a revision does not require identifying any scenario the text leaves unresolved.
An unaddressed scenario is a gap in coverage, whereas a conflated distinction is over-inclusive uniform treatment of cases the rule does address.
Both score whether a specific, adoptable alternative is put forward rather than bare objection; the drafting-parameter language sets a similar bar to specific alternative approach.
Correcting what the proposal says and naming what it fails to say are complementary opposites, and a comment can do either alone.
Both score a specific step-by-step chain running through behavior or implementation to the claimed consequence, with identical zero anchors.
Both score an alternative concrete enough to implement, listing the same operative parameters such as thresholds, exemptions, and replacement text.
Proposing monitoring machinery and pinpointing a provision for revision are unrelated behaviors.

The first demands insider-level description of the existing workflow and where the proposal breaks, while the second credits abstract identification of responsible actors, dependencies, and failure modes.
The first requires a specific named rule, docket, or precedent, while the second also credits unnamed duplication, coordination burdens, and workflow interactions across agencies.
Quantification against a baseline is unrelated to tracing second-order effects across connected systems.
The second additionally requires an identified rule-text target, so a precise but unanchored requested change scores high on the first and low on the second.
Describing an unaddressed scenario need not quote or correct the proposal's wording, and a correction of a misstatement need not raise any scenario.
Both score whether specific groups bearing distinct costs or benefits are identified with the exposure mechanism explained, and both zero out on the undifferentiated public.
Engaging multiple provisions and explaining their operation is independent of supplying rule-specific numbers.
Cross-rule conflict identification and monitoring or verification design are unrelated contributions.
Both score whether the comment identifies the actors, systems, resources, and dependencies that determine whether the rule can actually be executed, versus treating implementation as automatic.
Both score a credible step-by-step mechanism from the requirement to concrete effects, with identical zero anchors of bare assertion.
Both score whether a concrete alternative regulatory design is described specifically enough to adopt, versus proposing nothing.
The first rewards engaging multiple provisions and explaining how they operate, with no revision required, while the second requires a concrete requested revision to an exact provision.
Explaining how proposed provisions operate does not require identifying an error, ambiguity, or misstatement in the agency's language.
